Target audience: High school students or undergraduate mathematics enthusiasts

Section: section_1 — The Hook: How many pieces?

Lecture lines:
Place points on a circle, connect every pair.
One point creates one slice.
Two points, two slices.
Three points, four slices.
Four points, eight slices.

Planned animations:
Draw a circle (#FFFFFF) and place 1 point (#FF0000). Fill circle with 1 region (#00FF00).
Add a 2nd point (#FF0000). Draw a chord (#FFFF00). Show 2 regions (#00FF00).
Add a 3rd point (#FF0000). Draw remaining chords (#FFFF00). Show 4 regions (#00FF00).
Add a 4th point (#FF0000). Draw remaining chords (#FFFF00). Show 8 regions (#00FF00).
Zoom out to show the collection of circles from n=1 to 4 side-by-side.

Section: section_2 — Pattern Recognition (The Trap)

Lecture lines:
The sequence is 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
Each step seems to double the last.
Predicting 32 is a natural trap.

Planned animations:
List the sequence: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 in a central text area (#FFFFFF).
Animate the number 16 doubling to a placeholder '32?' (#FFD700, bold).
Explain the pattern: '2 to the power of (n-1)' appearing below the sequence.

Section: section_3 — The Reality Check (n=6)

Lecture lines:
Try n equals six points.
The regions count reaches 31.
The doubling pattern fails here.

Planned animations:
Draw a circle with 6 dots (#FFFFFF) and all possible chords (#FFFF00).
Highlight intersection points (#FF0000) using circles. Count them.
Display the number 31 (#FF0000, large) replacing the guessed '32' (#00FF00, crossed out).

Section: section_4 — The Combinatorial Formula

Lecture lines:
Regions equal intersections plus chords plus one.
Formula: Choose four points plus two plus one.
Combinatorics define the structure precisely.
Each intersection adds a new region.
Each chord adds a new region too.

Planned animations:
Display formula R = C(n,4) + C(n,2) + 1 (#FFFFFF).
Visualize C(n,2) as new chords adding regions (#FFFF00).
Visualize C(n,4) as intersections of two chords adding an extra region (#00FF00).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: The Power of Proof

Lecture lines:
Never trust patterns without proof.
Mathematical truth requires rigorous verification.
The journey matters most.

Planned animations:
Display the full sequence: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31 (#FFFFFF).
Flash a 'Caution' icon (#FF0000) next to the sequence.
Type 'Verify, Don't Just Guess' (#FFFF00) below the sequence.
